title: wiretap: Match packets with the process blocks that precede them
description:
Follow-up to !26479 and the process-ID reuse discussion on !26518 (Guy's question about wraparound): how a packet's process ID is resolved to a Process Information Block when the ID has been reused.

So far `wtap_file_find_pib()` told the blocks for one process ID apart only by their start times against the packet's time stamp, and took the first block when every start time was later. That left two gaps: a writer that records no start times got no disambiguation at all, and a disagreement between the process clock and the capture clock could match a packet with the wrong incarnation.

Every writer so far (dumpcap in !26518, Apple's tcpdump) describes a process before the first packet it attributes to it, so the position in the file is reliable evidence. Wiretap now records where each block ends, the frame dissector passes the packet's file offset through `epan_find_process_info()`, and only the blocks that precede the packet are considered, unless none does (a writer that puts the blocks at the end of the file, which the second pass then sees). Among those, the start times decide as before; when all of them are later than the packet, the last block before it is taken rather than the first.

**API**: `wtap_add_pib()` takes the block's end offset; `wtap_file_find_pib()`, `epan_find_process_info()` and the packet provider's `find_process_info` take the packet's file offset (-1 to consider every block). All in-tree callers updated; the functions were added in !26471 and !26479 and are unreleased.

**Tests**: a new generated capture interleaves the blocks with the packets (`test/captures/_gen_process_info_blocks.py`) and covers: two blocks without start times (file order decides), all start times later than the packet (the last block before it), a later block that must not be chosen when an earlier one fits, and a block after the packet (found on the second pass). One expectation of the existing reuse test changes accordingly: a packet time-stamped before every block's start now matches the last block before it, not the first.

Built and tested on Windows, Linux (GCC, Clang + code checks, ASAN) and macOS.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01MeQMmftoMWrDyC8HdFk7sT

commits_data.message:
wiretap: Match packets with the process blocks that precede them

A process information block describes a process that reused an ID as a
new one, and wtap_file_find_pib() told such blocks apart only by their
start times against the packet's time stamp, falling back to the first
block when every start time was later. A writer that records no start
times got no disambiguation at all, and one whose process clock and
capture clock disagree could match a packet with the wrong incarnation.

Every writer so far, dumpcap and Apple's tcpdump, describes a process
before the first packet it attributes to it, so use the position in the
file: wiretap now records where each block ends, the frame dissector
passes the packet's file offset, and only the blocks that precede the
packet are considered, unless none does (a writer that puts them at the
end, which the second pass then sees). Among those the start times
decide as before; when all of them are later than the packet, the last
block before it is taken rather than the first, as its position is the
evidence left.

Add a generated capture with the blocks interleaved with the packets,
and tests for the cases: no start times, all start times later, a later
block that must not be chosen, and a block after the packet.

Related to #1184 and #17525.
